correctness.rationale: For n=3q+1, q>=1, a selected-edge graph H on K_n totally dominates L(K_n) iff it has at most one isolated ground vertex and no isolated single-edge component. Component and forest counting force exactly one ground isolate plus q disjoint P3 components at size 2q. On deleting edge ab from path a-b-c, valid replacements other than ab are ac, ub, uc (u the isolate); exactly ac and ub meet ab. Thus degrees are 6q for unrestricted exchanges and 4q for slides. Center-changing slides together with singleton/leaf swaps generate all rooted triple partitions: connectedness follows, and S_n-transitivity and handshake give N=n!/(2^q q!), 3qN and 2qN edges. Independently enumerated all length-2q open-neighborhood total dominators for n=4,7, obtaining N=12,630 with uniform degree pairs (6,4),(12,8). This is corroboration, not the all-q proof.

value.rationale: Minimum total domination determines a natural family of optimal monitoring configurations; reachability via local moves is not mechanically implied by its cardinality. The theorem computes all local moves and gives an infinite family of connected regular exchange and stricter slide graphs, quantifying exactly qN non-slide moves. It is a complete structural reconfiguration result, not a numerical restatement of the known static count.

limitations: Only n=3q+1, q>=1; does not determine diameter, spectrum, or other congruence classes.
